newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INTERPELLATION DEBATE TO START SEP 25 1400.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INTERPELLATION DEBATE TO START SEP 25 1400.

text.p: Debate in the Finnish parliament on the interpellation submitted by the opposition Centre Party will start on Wednesday at 1400 (1100 GMT), a parliament spokesman said on Monday.

It had not yet been decided which cabinet minister will give the government's response to the interpellation, an official at the prime minister's office said, adding that Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen will be present during the debate.
An interpellation debate is always followed by a vote of confidence in the government. The left-right-green coalition's five parties in the have 142 seats in the 200-strong house.

In the interpellation, the Centre Party said the government was siding with the well-to-do who are fortunate to have a secure income, and widening the gap between them and the poor by cutting social benefits and allowing mass-unemployment to continue.
"The government has failed completely to reduce unemployment although it explicitly set halving unemployment as its main goal," the Centre Party said.
It also criticised the government for discriminating against families with small children, for introducing tax cuts favouring high-wage earners and forgetting pensioners.
With municipal and European parliament elections around the corner on October 20, the number of MPs eager to participate in the interpellation debate is likely to be quite big, officials said.
The vote of confidence was likely to be held at the earliest on Friday, September 27, the parliament spokesman said.
